messages.content:
Build the app described below in an existing Next.js 16 project (App Router, React 19, strict TypeScript).

Stack: Mantine (`@mantine/core` 9) is set up with its Next.js App Router provider, styles and PostCSS preset; `@mantine/hooks`, `form`, `dates`, `charts`, `notifications`, `modals`, `spotlight` and `@tabler/icons-react` are installed, and the Mantine documentation is in the `docs/` folder, which you can read (start with `docs/README.md`).

Task: Lumen needs a command palette. Inside a shared app layout with three screens (a dashboard at `/`, projects at `/projects`, members at `/members`), pressing Ctrl+K (Cmd+K on a Mac) opens a palette with a search field. Results are grouped under "Pages" (the three screens), "Actions" ("Create project", "Invite member", "Toggle theme") and "Recent" (three recently opened projects). Typing filters every group; arrow keys move the highlight and Enter runs it. "Invite member" opens a dialog with an email field. A visible button in the header (with the shortcut shown next to it) opens the palette too, so it works on phones.

- Write as many files as the app needs, under `app/`, `components/` or `lib/`. Do not change any file that already exists in the project except `app/page.tsx`. The root layout, global styles and the stack's standard providers already exist. You can read the project's existing files under `project/`.
- Put "use client" at the top of every file that uses state, effects or event handlers.
- Use realistic placeholder content defined in the files (no lorem ipsum). Load nothing from the network: no external image, font or API URLs.
- The app must type-check under strict TypeScript, pass `next build`, and render every route without console errors.
- Make it responsive from phone to desktop, and accessible.

content.text: Next, the details on the Modal, color scheme and form that I'll use for the Invite dialog and theme toggle.

The Spotlight needs to be mounted inside the shared layout, so I'll put the layout into a route group. Only `app/page.tsx` can be edited, so I can't wrap it with a layout file at `app/`. Instead I'll build a shared `AppFrame` component in `components/` that each page uses, which works whether or not nested layouts are used.

My design plan:

-   `lib/data.ts`: typed data.
-   `components/AppFrame.tsx`: client component with AppShell (header with logo, nav, search button + Kbd, theme toggle; navbar drawer on mobile via Burger), mounting `CommandPalette` and the invite dialog.
-   `components/CommandPalette.tsx`: uses Spotlight with groups and `router.push`.
-   `components/InviteMemberModal.tsx`: Modal with a `useForm` email field.
-   Pages and screens for dashboard, projects, members.

For the shared layout, I'll use route groups: `app/(app)/layout.tsx` for projects/members, but `app/page.tsx` is at the root, so it can't join that group. Each page will therefore wrap itself in `AppFrame`, which would remount on navigation. The cleaner option is a nested layout for `/projects` and `/members` plus the dashboard rendering `AppFrame` directly, but that splits the layout in two places. I'll go with a single approach, which is every page rendering `<AppFrame>`; the Spotlight store is global so state is preserved enough.

A few details to handle:

-   Spotlight `shortcut="mod + K"` is the default, so I'll keep it explicit.
-   "Create project" will open a modal (via `@mantine/modals`) with a name field and show a notification, as it needs to do something useful.
-   "Toggle theme" uses `useMantineColorScheme` and `useComputedColorScheme`. The icon uses CSS-only `lightHidden`/`darkHidden` to avoid hydration mismatches.
-   The shortcut label depends on the OS, so I'll render `Ctrl K` on first render and switch after mount with `useOs({ getValueInEffect: true })`.
-   "Recent" will be three most recently updated projects: APP, WEB, API.
-   Action IDs/labels, filtering across groups: the default filter matches label/description/keywords and drops empty groups.

Dates should format deterministically to avoid hydration mismatches, so I'll use a fixed `en-US` locale with `timeZone: "UTC"`.

); } ``` ## data prop You can use the `data` prop to automatically generate table rows from an array of React nodes. The `data` prop accepts an object with the following properties: * `head` – an array of React nodes (`React.ReactNode[]`) to render `Table.Th` in `Table.Thead` * `foot` – an array of React nodes (`React.ReactNode[]`) to render `Table.Th` in `Table.Tfoot` * `body` - an array of arrays of React nodes (`React.ReactNode[][]`) to render `Table.Td` in `Table.Tbody` * `caption` – a React node to render `Table.Caption` ```tsx import { Table, TableData } from '@mantine/core'; const tableData: TableData = { caption: 'Some elements from periodic table', head: ['Element position', 'Atomic mass', 'Symbol', 'Element name'], body: [ [6, 12.011, 'C', 'Carbon'], [7, 14.007, 'N', 'Nitrogen'], [39, 88.906, 'Y', 'Yttrium'], [56, 137.33, 'Ba', 'Barium'], [58, 140.12, 'Ce', 'Cerium'], ], }; function Demo() { return ; } ``` ## Sticky header Set `stickyHeader` to make the table header sticky. To customize the top position of the header, use the `stickyHeaderOffset` prop: it is useful when you have a fixed header in your application.
